title: (a) Derive JWT-SVID TTL from the source, not a constant
description:
hire-core/src/signer.rs:203 hardcodes exp = now + 300 for every JWT-SVID regardless of what backs it. persona-3tly.6 already establishes that a TTL means different things per source: where departure is observable a TTL is a backstop and can be generous; where it is not, the TTL is the ENTIRE safety margin and should be short.

Layer (a) of the persona-3tly.7 decision. This is the only layer that reaches a stock SPIFFE consumer that self-verifies against the published JWKS and never calls back.

Depends on persona-5s4b.24, which already flags the hardcoded 300s and the untyped serde_json::Value the signer takes.

WATCH THE SKEW FLOOR recorded on persona-3tly.7: seconds-scale exp is safe for local consumption over the Unix socket because there is no skew, and unsafe for a token forwarded to an off-host relying party whose skew tolerance is conventionally minutes. A single TTL cannot serve both. Whether that means two token shapes, or presence being withheld from forwardable tokens, is the decision this bead has to make rather than inherit.
acceptance_criteria: TTL is a function of the backing source's departure-detection capability; no hardcoded constant; the forwarded-token skew case is explicitly answered.
